description: Which accounts are effectively pinned, and in which order. Stored are the switch "status icons on" and an ordered list of account ids. Rule: (1) with the switch off, nothing is pinned, whatever is stored. (2) Otherwise keep the stored ids that name an existing usage account; an id of a credit account never qualifies (credit balances are a separate kind of account), an id whose account is gone is dropped, and an id stored twice counts once. A usage account without a reading yet does qualify (its icon shows the dash). (3) Order the kept ids by the app's account order, not by the order they were pinned in. (4) Take the first three. The interface refuses a fourth pin; this rule still truncates defensively. Expected lists are written by hand from this rule, not generated from either implementation. Both platforms read this file unchanged with a strict decoder: an unknown or missing key fails the suite.
schema: vectors: array of { name: string (unique, says what the case proves); enabled: boolean (the stored switch); pinned: array of string (the stored ids, in stored order); usageAccounts: array of { id: string; hasReading: boolean } in the app's account order (hasReading states whether the account has a reading yet; it never changes the answer); creditAccounts: array of string (ids of existing credit accounts); expected: array of string (the effective pinned ids, in order, at most three) }.

vectors.name: four stored ids keep the first three in account order
a stored id whose account is gone is dropped
four stored ids with one gone keep the other three
a credit account id never qualifies
a usage account without a reading qualifies
order follows account order, not pin order
an id stored twice counts once
feature off pins nothing, whatever is stored
no accounts at all pins nothing
